title: Derived tensor comparison for arbitrary ringed topoi
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to the universe of module sheaves, with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits. Equip it with a ring map $u^{-1}R\to S$. Write $D(R)$ and $D(S)$ for the unbounded derived categories of the abelian categories of sheaves of modules over these rings [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Module pullback is $u^*M=S\otimes_{u^{-1}R}u^{-1}M$, using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; $Lu^*:D(R)\to D(S)$ is its total left derived functor, computed by applying $u^*$ to K-flat resolutions with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pullback]. Here a sheaf of modules is flat when tensoring with it is exact [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. If $P$ is K-flat with flat terms, then $u^*P$ is K-flat with flat terms. Derived tensor is computed by the total tensor complex [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] of K-flat resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. For all $F,G\in D(R)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 Lu^*(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}G)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*F\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}Lu^*G
$$
in $D(S)$, natural simultaneously in $F$ and $G$.

proof.text: Use the existing ringed-topos pullback preservation theorem to obtain K-flatness and termwise site-flatness of every pulled-back representative.

The complex comparison is the composite of quotient comparisons and the specified counit. For the independent-site-universe interface, use the published K-flat tensor computation. For the older equal-universe interface, that module imports the interface being proved: instead the existing ringedTopoiDerivedPullback theorem supplies a derived pullback with invertible counit on K-flat flat-term representatives. Uniqueness of left-derived functors transports this to the supplied LF and epsilon. The total tensor model supplies K-flatness and flat terms for tensors. In both interfaces, transport flatness along siteSheafTensorRightIso without assuming the coefficient map is flat.

The given canonical ordinary comparison yields the total chain isomorphism. Prove its naturality by testing each degree on every tensor summand and using the inverse ordinary tensor naturality square.

Use independent-universe K-flat resolutions and the explicit site tensor/right tensor isomorphism to resolve every homotopy object. The resolving-representative restriction lemma gives fully faithful restriction in two variables; transport along the canonical quotient comparison.

Apply tensorComparisonDescent to the explicit natural complex comparison and total tensor isomorphism. Its square gives existence. Proof irrelevance identifies the target representative membership witnesses; the same square and fully faithful restriction give uniqueness.
